experiments.description: Simulated amplitude estimation for a European call option using a log-normal spot-price distribution and varying the number of sampling qubits.

algorithm.variant: standard amplitude estimation with quantum phase estimation

hyperparameters.distribution_truncation: three standard deviations around the mean

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the undiscounted expected payoff E[max(0, S_T - K)] for a European call option.

problem_instance.description: European call option on a single underlying asset with a log-normal terminal price distribution.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes-Merton log-normal distribution; example parameters S0=2, sigma=10%, r=4%, T=300/365; strike K=2.0.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Truncate the terminal price distribution to a finite interval and discretize it into a 3-qubit register.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Map measured phase-estimation outcome y to a = sin^2(y*pi/M) and recover the option price from the encoded amplitude.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct the A operator from a loaded log-normal distribution and a piecewise-linear payoff encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare estimated option price against analytical Black-Scholes-Merton value and classical Monte Carlo baseline.

speedup_claims.conditions: standard amplitude estimation with quantum phase estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the estimator error scales as O(1/M) versus O(M^-1/2) for Monte Carlo; the plotted results are simulated.

experiments.description: Simulated amplitude estimation for a basket call option on three correlated assets, comparing estimation error against Monte Carlo as the number of sampling qubits increases.

algorithm.variant: standard amplitude estimation with quantum phase estimation

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the undiscounted expected payoff E[max(0, w·S - K)] for a basket call option.

problem_instance.description: Basket option on three identical, equally weighted underlying assets with correlated multivariate log-normal terminal distribution.

dataset_specification.description: Three identical assets with the same parameters as Fig. 3; correlations rho12=rho13=rho23=0.8; strike K=2.0.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Load multivariate log-normal distribution and compute weighted sum of asset prices before payoff evaluation.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Compare amplitude-estimation error to Monte Carlo error at the 8/pi^2 confidence interval.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare multivariate distribution and weighted-sum operator.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate error scaling versus number of samples and compare to Monte Carlo over 10,000 simulations per sample size.

speedup_claims.conditions: basket option on three correlated assets; amplitude estimation with phase estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: Comparison is based on simulated AE error versus Monte Carlo error over 10,000 simulations per sample size at the 8/π^2 confidence interval.

experiments.description: Simulated amplitude estimation for an arithmetic-average Asian call option with two time steps.

algorithm.variant: standard amplitude estimation with quantum phase estimation

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the undiscounted expected payoff E[max(0, S_bar - K)] where S_bar is the arithmetic average of the asset price over time.

problem_instance.description: Single-asset path-dependent Asian option with two discretized time points up to maturity.

dataset_specification.description: Asset price at t=Delta t and t=T, with Delta t=T/2; log-normal transition model with parameters from the BSM setup.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Represent the asset price at each time step in separate registers and compute the arithmetic average using a weighted-sum operator.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Use amplitude estimation to infer the expected payoff from the measured amplitude.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare multivariate time-slice distribution and average-price register.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover option value from the estimated amplitude.

speedup_claims.conditions: path-dependent Asian option pricing via amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper describes the circuit construction but does not report a numerical comparison plot or table for this Asian option.

experiments.description: Simulated amplitude estimation for a knock-in barrier option with two time steps and a barrier checked at both times.

algorithm.variant: standard amplitude estimation with quantum phase estimation

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the undiscounted expected payoff E[max(0, S_T - K) * 1{exists t: S_t >= B}] for a knock-in barrier option.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Barrier condition implemented via comparator qubits and logical OR over time steps.

problem_instance.description: Single-asset knock-in barrier option with two discretized time points and a barrier at both time steps.

dataset_specification.description: Asset from Fig. 3; two time steps T/2 and T; 2 qubits per time step; strike K=1.9; barrier B=2.0.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Load the multivariate time-slice distribution, compute barrier indicators at each time step, and OR them into a single barrier flag.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Compare estimated option price to Monte Carlo with 100,000 paths.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare time-sliced distribution and barrier comparator circuits.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Read out the estimated payoff from the amplitude-estimation output.

speedup_claims.conditions: barrier option pricing with amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The figure shows a simulated AE estimate compared against a Monte Carlo benchmark with 100,000 paths; no explicit numeric error value is stated in text.

experiments.description: Hardware experiment on IBM Q Tokyo evaluating amplitude-estimation-based pricing of a European call option using the Suzuki et al. no-phase-estimation variant, with readout mitigation and CNOT error mitigation.

algorithm.variant: amplitude estimation without phase estimation (Suzuki et al.)

hyperparameters.truncation: three standard deviations around the mean

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff of a European call option using a 2-qubit discretization of the terminal asset price and a payoff qubit.

problem_instance.description: European call option on a single asset, evaluated for eight different initial spot prices while keeping all other parameters fixed.

dataset_specification.description: Log-normal terminal distribution with S0 varied from 1.8 to 2.5 in increments of 0.1; strike K=1.74; sigma=40%; r=5%; T=40/365.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the log-normal distribution into four values and map them to two uncertainty qubits; construct the A and QA circuits for each spot price.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation over measured probabilities from A|0> and QA|0> to infer the option price; apply readout correction and Richardson extrapolation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare the 2-qubit log-normal distribution and piecewise-linear payoff angles.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use calibration matrix inversion for readout mitigation and second-order Richardson extrapolation over 18, 54, and 90 CNOT-gate circuits.

classical_baselines.value: exact option price / simulated probability baseline

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a hardware feasibility and error-mitigation experiment, not a speedup benchmark.
